signals.evidence: Bre'em (Matte Asher): Community leaders report distrust in politicians and military; promised secure border did not materialize
Bre'em: Residents in continuous shelter stay due to absence of individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); unclear if shelters designed for extended occupancy
Bre'em: Farmers report limited armored field protection booths (מיגוניות) relative to area size; request regular food supply
Bre'em: Lack of protected spaces for educational/social activities; no suitable public space available
Bre'em: צח"י (community resilience unit) training and volunteer reinforcement requested; informal activities began today
Bre'em: Elderly population receiving community-level response; informal activities initiated
Bre'em: Concern about business collapse (pizzeria); gap in education personnel; proposal to fill gap with reserve soldiers
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef: Narrative of staying; accompanied by difficulties; variation in reports about work departure
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef: Many residents lack individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); shelters not in optimal condition; some residents find shelters too distant
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef: Increase in calls to emergency hotline 106
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef: Elderly population in distress; difficulty reaching safe rooms; sometimes injured
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef: Need for military presence (soldier-teachers/מורות חיילות) identified for public messaging
Avdon/Ma'ale Yosef (Bre'em): Residents not leaving; community coordinator recruiting volunteers
Avdon: Additional armored field protection booths (מיגוניות) provided; צח"י community coordinator recruiting volunteers
Avdon: Women's evening and activities for adults held; informal activities ongoing
Avdon: Not all elderly have individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters distant; unable to reach shelters in time
Liman: Central distress—lack of activities for children; request for soldier-teacher support
Liman: Those able to use individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); difficulty protecting farmers' security
Liman: Known protection gaps; all in process of receiving response; צח"י functioning well overall; request for soldier-teachers
Granot HaGalil/Ma'ale Yosef (Bre'em): Sense of fatigue and erosion (שחיקה) from ongoing situation

Granot HaGalil: Community resilience expressed as willingness to enable what is possible without distraction; majority of population returned; young functioning population; coping discourse; basic youth activity; readiness unit present; community communication without toxic discourse; good relationship with council and Home Front Command

Granot HaGalil: Protection gaps; elderly lack protection; צח"י not operating at full capacity; no designated guardian for elderly and people with disabilities; welfare services not connected to this population; gap in mapping of entire population due to צח"י not fully activated
Granot HaGalil: Ongoing erosion (שחיקה) noted in both veteran population with high resilience and newer population with basic resilience
Even Menahem/Ma'ale Yosef (Bre'em): Residents (Moshe and Yiron) state: 'We are mentally ill people living here' (אנחנו חולי נפש שאנו גרים כאן)
Even Menahem: Significant criticism toward the council
Even Menahem: Leadership functioning under difficulties

Even Menahem: צח"י not fully operational; no organized infrastructure for mapping needs and difficulties; urgent need for short-term resilience strengthening alongside long-term solutions; community under difficulty and deep erosion; limited number of volunteers
Even Menahem: Community involvement and mutual aid when needed present
Mattat/Ma'ale Yosef (Bre'em): Community cohesion significantly strengthened; couple exited public shelter (serving as youth club) to conduct memorial singing rehearsals for Mati Kaspi
Mattat: Families without individual safe rooms (ממ"ד); need for sewage infrastructure repair; need for relief activities for children and families
Mattat: Community coordinator working at full capacity
Batzet/Matte Asher (Bre'em): Community dealing with crisis; strong leadership and cooperation among different role-holders
Batzet: Beginning to enter emergency routine; activities for young ages; work in cycles due to lack of suitable shelters; farmers working and people going to work
Batzet: Children and youth at home using Zoom with limited success; difficulty implementing education frameworks; workers not arriving
Batzet: צח"י active; volunteers present; soldier-teachers; army education core (גרעין נח"ל); assistance with transportation for army education core to function
Batzet: Difficulties with youth revealed complexities of substance and alcohol use
Batzet: Light renovation of shelter to serve educational activities; request to resilience center for activities; request to defense department for equipment

Psuta (Bre'em): Overall resilience present but political instability affecting it; people in emergency routine but more free; training and learning for essential authority and medical workers; relief workshops and learning center for high schools; student council activity

Psuta: Shortage of one shelter unsuitable for use; volunteer network present but weak attendance; not arriving with only basic training; clubs for elderly and special needs closed and difficult to visit; experiencing loneliness and difficulty; welfare struggling to reach all residents for visits
Psuta: Extensive informal activities conducted by education department; request to Ministry of Education for computer allocation
Psuta: Request to defense department for equipment for protection screening
Alkosh/Ma'ale Yosef (Bre'em): Population obedient to Home Front Command policy and directives

Alkosh: Elderly population struggling to reach protected areas; general apathy expressed in lack of volunteering for leisure activities and community life; no community cohesion; no motivating leadership for action

Alkosh: צח"י includes only the chair, no additional functionaries; limited enrichment activities for children; community lacks the backbone of community leadership—recommendation for welfare department to work on leadership and joint community activity dimensions

Horfish (Bre'em): Authority broadcasting resilience, high control in community; strong community; full emergency routine; private businesses opening; council-related matters showing policy hardening by authority head
Horfish: No activity even in public shelters; 30% without protection but no protection problems in public institutions and public areas—gap closed
Horfish: Loneliness; frameworks not working for elderly, women, and special needs population—all cancelled, some minimal activity via Zoom

Horfish: Social services department creating personal contact with population needing assistance; strengthening psycho-social response for children and adults; utilizing resilience centers and resources

Horfish: Request for assistance to businesses and tourism; computers for children in education system; equipment for first aid screening; strengthening connection of local council with Horfish and Psuta

Kibbutz Eilon/Matte Asher (Bre'em): Evacuation created dependency among some residents for basic needs such as cleaning, repairs, food; some residents still struggling to return to autonomous functioning
Kibbutz Eilon: Sense of broken community cohesion following evacuation in Iron Swords war; residents more autonomous and less engaged in community activities

Kibbutz Eilon: Shelter quality low—old systems, stuffy; no protection in local clinic—need to restore medical/clinic response; many essential workers with uncertainty due to lack of answers and solutions for their children
Kibbutz Eilon: Informal education—activity present but relatively limited because instructors partly not kibbutz residents and did not return
Kibbutz Eilon: Promotion of resilience lectures in primary care clinic; professional support especially in community management in routine and emergency; organizational consulting

Ya'ara: Those without individual safe rooms (ממ"ד) self-evacuated; those with shelters shelter in place; public shelters serve worshippers and informal frameworks but too small to contain activities or defense policy does not permit (over 50)

Ya'ara: צח"י attempting population survey but only 5 out of over 250 families; loneliness, fatalistic because no one will help evacuate them to safe room when needed (moving slowly); request to social services for elderly assistance; request to ease number allowed in shelter; light-to-moderate shelter repairs; need to connect civil-religious public organizations to secular community; need for local government representative to assist with anchor lists
Manot: No frameworks; desire for informal education or opening frameworks for kindergarten-elementary in community areas; not working except remotely; many mobilized to reserves

Manot: צח"י present with organizations bringing supplies and services via WhatsApp; residents caring for each other within family framework; compared to closer communities to fence, they enjoy organization support; less fear of reaching them to help
Manot: Elderly not apparent; absence of aid packages in current round noted by residents

Netu'a: Residents do not want evacuation except parents with children (parents want, children resist); veterans want to stay home; families in homes trying to live under emergency routine; צח"י in contact with residents providing response to weakened populations; resilience present as long as IDF does its job; economic uncertainty; community in coping and growth processes pre-war; after return from evacuation, positive community recovery and resilience evident; formal and informal leadership performing trust-building processes with community; internal forces and צח"י, rabbi, readiness unit working in good communication

Netu'a: Recommendation to encourage community preparation with authority support to provide community, cultural, and educational responses for all age groups from community forces; strengthen community צח"י and train community emergency coordinator and practice with council; connect business owners to service in cluster of authorities for business promotion

Shetula: Nervousness about crisis; erosion of role-holders; resilience not high but internal forces holding community; outside volunteers coming to help; elderly unable to leave home, need supplies of medicine and food; little informal education activity with desire to increase responses

Shetula: צח"י team contacting all weakened populations with emphasis on widows and elderly; help bringing medicine and food through coordinated purchases among residents or volunteers; צח"י in contact managing needs of adults; difficulty of elderly is loneliness; 50% of residents want to refresh, not evacuate

Shetula: Recommendation to encourage community, cultural, and educational responses for all age groups from community forces and outside; use outside volunteering to provide relief and reduce burden on leadership and volunteering teams, especially to help elderly and singles not feel alone; dialogue with community bodies in authority about encouraging volunteering activity and accessible relief culture for residents
Arab El-Aramsha: Shelters not providing sufficient response; no activities for children during Ramadan
Arab El-Aramsha: Residents filming during alerts

Arab El-Aramsha: Recommendation to deepen mapping and meeting with role-holders; holding preparations to provide community, cultural, and educational responses for all age groups; encourage establishment of צח"י

Adamit/Matte Asher (Bre'em): Most residents in community; readiness unit needing refresher; frustrations and distrust toward army; צח"י operating toward elderly and special needs; parents with small children without protection; parents exhausted but not using resilience services; mobilizing youth to help in kibbutz; caring for people staying in shelters

Adamit: Recommendation to allocate resources for relief activities; promote child education activities and support for mobilized and essential workers from community; allocate resources for relief outside kibbutz for day or two; visit by senior commanders for trust-building dialogue
Kibbutz Snir/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Narrative of resilience; high mutual aid; informal activities especially afternoons in shelters; use of WhatsApp groups

Kibbutz Snir: Shortage of armored field protection booth in expansion neighborhood; no siren coverage; need for soldier-teachers and security personnel; elderly difficulty reaching shelters due to 0 alert time and doctor almost not coming; welfare—logistical aspects for reserve families; problem of shared military-civilian command—need separation

Beit Hillel/Mevuot Hermon (Hiram): Expansion residents more hysterical (former Kiryat Shmona residents); no intention to leave; students present who would not want to leave; relief activities—one to one-and-a-half hours; work continuity variable; functional continuity 60%; no extensive activity for elderly; protection gaps in elderly club; youth club without standard protection; children's shelter—infrastructure problem; individual safe room (ממ"ד) situation improved significantly; shopping trips to Kiryat Shmona; צח"י—no chair; limited volunteer network but operating by sub-teams; relief activity for elderly; relief activity for youth and children; resilience—two psychologists on site
Beit Hillel: Recommendation for reinforcement of female soldiers
Dafna/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Population coping; informal network operating; no protection gaps
Dafna: Emergency team and resilience team—urgent need for צח"י commander; elderly—loneliness problem

Me'ayan Baruch/Galil Elyon (Hiram): No desire to evacuate; strong community and strong authority; lack of armored field protection booths at bus station and two at playgrounds; elderly and welfare population being treated; economic concern pressing; request to finish mission in Lebanon; population with disabilities receiving response; lack of standard protection in informal education framework; need for soldier-teachers; messaging—what is permitted and what is forbidden

Kibbutz Dan/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Strong community coping; no protection in community buildings; use of community resources including צח"י; response to population with disabilities and elderly; informal activities ongoing; messaging—clarifying directives; help with personnel for community activity; shelter repair for continuous stay; siren check

Mishgav Am/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Most not ready to leave; took in six new families; doing activities for children; request for reinforcement of 2 soldier-teachers; functional continuity; צח"י—four residents; community action present; optimal response to elderly; residents with psychological trauma from war and evacuation; not all understand this will be long; lack of firefighters and צח"י team; request for relief; soldier-teachers as much as possible; prioritize protection
Mishgav Am: People tired and not sleeping well at night

Manara/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Strong community; relief activities starting tomorrow; significant protection gaps; army education core on mission; volunteers; preparatory program; strong צח"י; lack of welfare department—not staffed; regular צח"י meetings; elderly—no meetings due to lack of public space; difficulty descending stairs; age-based division; reinforcement of soldier-teachers to prevent erosion of education volunteers; support for relief; exit for refreshment

Tzabyon: Many relief activities for children and youth; some tired of alerts and returned to sleeping at home; emphasis on community cohesion and not evacuating; צח"י working well; volunteers hosting relief workshops; community resilience initiatives amazing

Tzabyon: Agriculture—missing armored field protection booth; old neighborhood—no individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); only one shelter for entire neighborhood; false alerts lowering resilience; need for protection reinforcement
Karem Ben Zimra: Transfer of model of action to children, parents, and צח"י team; relief for elderly; higher presence in community; round table of government ministries with צח"י
Kfar Giladi/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Narrative of strong community against neglect of state and denial of status as border community

Kfar Giladi: Relief for elderly within protected space; lack of ability to respond to ages 0-6; significant protection gaps; shelters not containing all residents without protection; volunteer network for elderly; challenge with bedridden patients without ability to protect; increase in calls to community resilience team; youth wandering; worsening of mental health condition; messaging and conveying sense that IDF is with us
